title: Particulate Nature of Matter
seo_title: Particulate Nature of Matter Class 8 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 7)
standard_code: Class 8, Curiosity Chapter 7: Particulate Nature of Matter
standard_text: Matter is made of tiny particles with spaces between them; particles are always moving and attract each other; diffusion and the effect of temperature; arrangement and movement of particles in solids, liquids and gases; changes of state, melting and boiling points; sublimation; expansion on heating (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 7).

key_big: Matter is made of tiny, moving particles.
key_sub: Solids: close and fixed. Liquids: close and sliding. Gases: far apart and free.
body_html:
How to think about it

All matter is made of tiny particles with spaces between them. The particles are always moving and attract one another. They spread and mix by diffusion, which is fastest in gases and faster when it is hotter: a crystal of potassium permanganate colours all the water, and the smell of hot food travels quickly.

In solids particles are packed closely and only vibrate, so solids have a fixed shape and volume. In liquids they slide past one another, so liquids flow. In gases they move freely and far apart, so gases fill their container and can be compressed. Heating gives particles energy, causing melting, boiling and expansion; camphor sublimes directly into vapour.

Example

Where is diffusion fastest?

gas particles move fastest

Answer: in gases

Example

Can a gas be compressed?

large spaces between particles

Answer: yes, easily

Common mistakes

  • Thinking dissolved sugar is destroyed.
  • Saying particles stop moving in solids.
  • Thinking a liquid has a fixed shape.
